questions.prompt: A session has events with seq 0, 1, 2, 4. What does this tell a reader?
options: Event 3 was ignored by the model
An event was lost, because sequence numbers never skip
Event 4 came from a different session
The record is normal, because numbers can skip after a tool call
questions.explanation: append sets seq to the list length, so the numbers always run 0, 1, 2, 3 with no gap. A missing 3 means an event is lost.

questions.prompt: Why does append copy the data through JSON before storing it?
options: So the event takes fewer tokens
So the model can read it as JSON
So the record can always be saved and a caller's later changes cannot reach it
So two events can share one sequence number
questions.explanation: The JSON copy is a separate object, so later changes by the caller do not change the record. Data JSON cannot hold never enters it, so the record can always be saved.

questions.prompt: Why do turns and steps get their own start and end events?
options: So a reader can tell a finished turn from one that stopped part way
Because the model needs them in every request
Because append refuses a tool result without them
To make the sequence numbers start at 1
questions.explanation: A turn/start with no turn/end shows a turn that never finished. Without the boundary events, a reader could not tell the two cases apart.
